name: Chad Anheliger
event: UFC Fight Night: Buckley vs. Malott
summary: A 39-year-old Alberta bantamweight (13-8, 2-3 UFC) who hits hard with his right hand but is a soft spot for wrestlers: Strader, Grigoriou and Cody Gibson each took him down four or five times. Returns from nearly two years out, which he spent rehabbing a knee, against a submission-first grappler.

how_they_fight.Striking: Right-hand puncher who likes to bait opponents forward and load up; landed 85 of 155 significant strikes in his decision over Charalampos Grigoriou and dropped Jesse Strader twice before stopping him in the third. Offence gets one-dimensional (the right hand) when he is behind, per Cageside Press on the Gibson loss.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Can wrestle offensively when it suits him (5 of 12 takedowns and 7:37 of control in his Contender Series upset of Muin Gafurov; 4 of 8 against Jose Johnson), but his bottom game is mostly survival: he defended Cody Gibson's arm triangles and front chokes, yet ate 12:25 of control.
how_they_fight.Defense: Takedown defence is the hole: Gibson went 5 for 6, Grigoriou 4 for 5, Strader 4 for 7, Johnson 1 for 2 and then finished him. Never stopped by strikes in 21 pro fights; all six of his stoppage losses are submissions (three of them in round one early in his career, then rounds two and three).
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Slow burner in the UFC: his only UFC finish (Strader) came at 3:33 of round three and his last three KO/TKO wins overall were all in round three. Regionally he was a fast finisher (six of his ten stoppage wins came in round one). Goes hard in the third when behind (rocked Gibson late) but has also been submitted late (Johnson, R3 4:49). Two-year layoff and age 39 are real cardio and rust questions.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Experienced and tough; won the Gafurov fight as a +320 underdog by grinding. Tends to start patiently and leave himself needing a late rally.

patterns: Right hand as the main weapon; baits forward pressure
Late finisher: last three KO/TKO wins (Maclean, Hiestand, Strader) all in round 3
Gets taken down repeatedly and spends long stretches on his back
Never KO'd/TKO'd in 21 fights; 6 submission losses (R1 x3, R2 x1, R3 x2)
UFC fights: 3 of 5 went the distance; losses came by decision (Alateng, Gibson) and late submission (Johnson, R3 4:49)
concerns: Takedown defence (about 40% in our numbers) against a pure grappler
Nearly two years out with a knee rehab; 39 years old
Submission losses: six of his eight defeats
keys_to_beat: Take him down early and often; he struggles to get back up
Hunt the back and chokes: he has been submitted six times
Avoid standing in front of the right hand, especially in round 3

news.text: Per Cageside Press, he spent his layoff rehabbing a knee injury; an August Shanghai booking clashed with his wife's due date and a visa lapse ruled out Las Vegas, so he lands at home in Edmonton. Says his body is the best it has been.
Last fight: lost a unanimous decision to Cody Gibson in Edmonton (30-27, 30-27, 30-26) after being taken down 5 of 6 times.
